In Qianning 2, Xingmi held all of Huainan. Emperor Zhaozong issued an edict making him vice military governor of Huainan with full authority, commissioner of farming, observation, and disposal, Bearer of the Golden Bellow, acting Grand Mentor, Grand Councillor, concurrent administrator of Yangzhou metropolis, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Hongnong, with a nominal fief of three thousand households and a substantive enfeoffment of one hundred.

In Qianning 2, Xingmi held all of Huainan. Emperor Zhaozong issued an edict making him vice military governor of Huainan with full authority, commissioner of farming, observation, and disposal, with the privilege of opening an office with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, acting Grand Mentor, Grand Councillor, concurrent administrator of Yangzhou metropolis, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Hongnong, with a nominal fief of three thousand households and a substantive enfeoffment of one hundred.
開府儀同三司 and 上柱國 replace the unrelated Golden Bellow rendering and the understated rank.

In the second year of Qianning, Xingmi wholly possessed the Huainan region; Emperor Zhaozong then issued an edict appointing Xingmi vice commissioner of the Huainan military governorship with authority over military governorship affairs, commissioner of circuit farming, observation, and disposal within the jurisdiction, Bearer of the Golden Bellow and Grand Preceptor of the Palace, acting Grand Mentor, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, concurrent chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture, Pillar of the State, Prince of Hongnong commandery, with a fief of three thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of one hundred households.

In the second year of Qianning, Xingmi held all the lands of Huainan; Zhaozong then issued an edict granting Xingmi appointment as vice military governor of Huainan with authority over the military governorship, commissioner for land reclamation, observation, and disposal within the circuit, with the privilege of opening an office and honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, acting Grand Mentor, jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery, concurrent Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan governor's office, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Hongnong Commandery, with a fief of three thousand households and a substantive fief of one hundred households.
The corrected titles follow 開府儀同三司 and 上柱國 in the source.

Xu Wen rose to Merit Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Quells Disturbance, and Builds the State, Grand Chancellor, supreme commander of all armies, overall commander of all circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, farming and observation commissioner for Xuan, She, Chi, and neighboring prefectures, Bearer of the Golden Bellow, Acting Grand Preceptor, Secretariat Director, chief administrator of Jinling, and Prince of Donghai, with a nominal fief of ten thousand households and a substantive enfeoffment of five hundred.

Xu Wen rose to Merit Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Quells Disturbance, and Builds the State, Grand Chancellor, supreme commander of all armies, overall commander of all circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, farming and observation commissioner for Xuan, She, Chi, and neighboring prefectures, with the privilege of opening an office and honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Acting Grand Preceptor, Secretariat Director, chief administrator of Jinling, and Prince of Donghai, with a nominal fief of ten thousand households and a substantive enfeoffment of five hundred.
開府儀同三司 is an honorary privilege, not Bearer of the Golden Bellow.

Li Bian had earlier dreamed that Xu Wen carried him up a mountain. A little over a year later Wen died, and Bian had himself invested as Merit Minister Who Assists the Government and Builds the State, with charge of all internal and external affairs, Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Departments, acting Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Xuancheng.

During Dazhong, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui declared himself acting governor. Chao sent Shenzhi to besiege him. After more than a year the city ran out of food, Hui was killed, and the garrison surrendered. Chao then held all five prefectures of Fujian and the surrounding hills.

During Dashun, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui declared himself acting governor. Chao sent Shenzhi to besiege him. After more than a year the city ran out of food, Hui was killed, and the garrison surrendered. Chao then held all five prefectures of Fujian and the surrounding hills.
大順 is Dashun, not Dazhong.

During Dazhong, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui styled himself acting governor; Chao sent Shenzhi to lead troops against him. After more than a year the city's provisions were exhausted; they beheaded Hui and surrendered, and thereby fully possessed the five prefectures of Min and the mountain region.

During Dashun, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui styled himself acting governor; Chao sent Shenzhi to lead troops against him. After more than a year the city's provisions were exhausted; they beheaded Hui and surrendered, and thereby fully possessed the five prefectures of Min and the mountain region.
大順 is Dashun, not Dazhong.
